exact_semantic_question: When LIMIT_VALUE_NMBR is empty, is the row a numeric limit, report-only monitoring, or something else?
relation_contract: empty numeric limit must be classified before comparison; absence is not a denial

candidate_interpretations.statement: Empty LIMIT_VALUE_NMBR denotes a monitoring/reporting requirement with no numeric effluent limit in that limit slot (permit tables show 'Report' or 'N/A' for that column).

Empty LIMIT_VALUE_NMBR on one limit-type row for a parameter does not mean no numeric limit exists; the same permit and parameter may carry the numeric limit on a sibling row with populated LIMIT_VALUE_NMBR.
Empty LIMIT_VALUE_NMBR on WET retest rows denotes pass/fail reporting encoded as 0/1 rather than a concentration limit.

Empty LIMIT_VALUE_NMBR rows tied to WHEN DISCHARGING or geometric-mean reporting footnotes denote monitoring obligations whose numeric comparison applicability depends on conditions or aggregation not captured in LIMIT_VALUE_NMBR.
Empty LIMIT_VALUE_NMBR might reflect missing structured encoding rather than an established non-numeric classification, especially where permit text is not matched in this workspace.

retained_snippets.location: All 57 rows with empty LIMIT_VALUE_NMBR; field LIMIT_TYPE_CODE
retained_snippets.text: LIMIT_TYPE_CODE = ENF for all 57 empty-limit rows (51 with OPTIONAL_MONITORING_FLAG = N, 6 with Y).
retained_snippets.why_retained: Shows LIMIT_TYPE_CODE does not disambiguate empty LIMIT_VALUE_NMBR: every empty row is marked ENF even where permit text and DMR comments establish report-only, pass/fail, or conditional monitoring rather than a numeric concentration limit in that row.

contradictory_evidence: All 57 empty LIMIT_VALUE_NMBR rows carry LIMIT_TYPE_CODE='ENF', which construction.py treats as a known enforceability code, yet permit tables and DMR comments for many of these rows establish Report-only, pass/fail, or conditional monitoring rather than a numeric limit in that slot.

LIMIT_VALUE_TYPE_CODE is not a reliable sole classifier: Q1/Q2 rows are sometimes empty and sometimes populated for the same parameter (e.g., NM0020583 TSS has populated Q1/Q2 loading limits alongside empty geometric-mean-related flow/TDS rows), and C2 rows can be empty (report) while C3 sibling rows carry numeric limits for the same parameter.

Representative keys 3610840341|3600904607 and 3610840340|3600904607 are empty Q1/Q2 TSS rows with 'WHEN DISCHARGING.' while sibling C2/C3 rows for the same permit and parameter carry numeric limits 20 and 30 mg/L, so emptiness on those rows does not mean the parameter lacks a numeric limit.
known_limitations: No workspace codebook defines LIMIT_VALUE_TYPE_CODE (C1/C2/C3/Q1/Q2); classification cannot be resolved from structured fields alone.
No FY2025 dmr_measurements.csv rows have empty LIMIT_VALUE_NMBR, so measurement-period applicability of these permit-limit rows cannot be tested against reported values in this workspace slice.

Pass/fail WET retest semantics are established primarily via structured DMR_COMMENT_TEXT; farmington/final_permit.txt Part II defines test failure conceptually but does not reproduce the exact PASS=0/FAIL=1 DMR encoding in retrieved sections.
WHEN DISCHARGING rows require discharge-occurrence evidence not present in structured sources; classification as conditionally applicable monitoring remains partially unresolved per period.
Blank-comment empty-limit rows (18/57) require permit-text matching per parameter; not all parameters were cross-checked against documents within the 5-document budget.
